name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,460

clue.text: Bachelor pulsating with energy in domestic garment?

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor
'a-throb' means throbbing, beating rhythmically
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A single man, full of vigour, lounging at home in something comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: B + ATHROB + E gives BATHROBE; the question mark admits the definition is loose, since the garment is worn about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose gown worn around the house after bathing, so it is clothing for home use.

clue.text: Writer covering first half of stay in small restaurant

indicators.note: only the opening two of the four letters of the following word are kept
the pen wraps round the other piece, sitting on either side of it

blocks.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writing implement
the front half of the word stay

explanation.surface: An author dining during a short stay in a little eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like a person, but it is a pen: a Biro is the British everyday name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a modest, informal eating place, originally French, serving simple meals.

clue.text: Hear about situation with seconds to go in negotiation

indicators.note: seconds abbreviates to S, and every such letter must leave the word
about means around, so the legal word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: to try a case is to hear it in court
a seat is a site or location

explanation.surface: A judge listening to talk of a position, with time running out in tense talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the courtroom sense, as a judge hears a case; 'seconds' means every S goes, not a time limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement reached by negotiation between states, so the word stands loosely for the bargaining.

clue.text: Speech without limits or proportion

indicators.note: limits are the edges of a word, so its first and last letters go

blocks.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Talk that is boundless, or else kept in measure.
explanation.walkthrough: ORATION trimmed of its outer O and N leaves RATIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relation of one quantity to another, which is what a proportion expresses.

clue.text: Graduate put out a reluctance, not new, to accept a diploma

indicators.note: new abbreviates to N, and 'not' tells us to drop that letter
the jumbled group takes in an extra letter before it is rearranged
put out means disturbed or disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate grudgingly taking a certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: A RELUCTANCE loses its N, takes in another A, and is rearranged after BA.
explanation.definitionFit: The baccalaureate is a school-leaving qualification, as in the International Baccalaureate, awarded as a diploma.

clue.text: Crop, perhaps, I hoard for cultivation

indicators.note: cultivating means working the ground over, so the letters are turned and reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmer stockpiling a harvest for planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks agricultural, matching the cultivation; it is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is a very short haircut, one example of a hairdo, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Comic film showing a figure internally upset by model

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns things over, and internally limits that to the inner part of the number
by means next to, so the model is placed after

blocks.note: taken as written
a figure is a number
Jerry Hall is a famous model

explanation.surface: A shape, disturbed inside by a fashion model, in a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle IN of NINE flips, giving NNIE. Annie Hall is Woody Allen's 1977 comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Hall is a celebrated romantic comedy film directed by and starring Woody Allen.

clue.text: Paddy produces this waffle, say - getting light fuel?

blocks.note: a paddy is a flooded field where rice is grown
a waffle is a kind of batter cake

explanation.surface: An Irishman blathering on while stoking up with something light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' poses as an Irishman and 'waffle' as chatter; one is a field, the other a griddle cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice cake is a low-calorie puffed snack, so it is food (fuel for the body) that is light.

clue.text: Patience, maybe, required in work over time covering European racing event

indicators.note: the era wraps round the other letters, enclosing them
in a down entry over means placed above, so the work comes first

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time
E is the abbreviation for European
the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

explanation.surface: Extra hours on the job demand patience at a continental race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' looks like the virtue a long race needs; it is Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a light comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, and such a short light opera is an operetta.

clue.text: Cold in beginning of autumn I term largely doubtful

indicators.note: in places the cold letter inside the month
largely means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap
September is the month that begins autumn, abbreviated
taken as written
to term something is to call it

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether the autumn term will start chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like a school term beside autumn, but it is a verb meaning call.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptical means inclined to doubt or question claims, so it is a synonym for doubtful.

clue.text: Delicate and beautiful containing good colour - like a tea leaf?

indicators.note: the beautiful word holds the good letter inside it

blocks.note: light means delicate, gentle
fine can mean beautiful, handsome
G is the abbreviation for good
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A dainty, pretty tea leaf of fine colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea leaf' is rhyming slang for thief, a British usage; the surface pretends it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea leaf is a thief in Cockney rhyming slang, and a thief is light-fingered, quick to pilfer.

clue.text: Small, specialised group engaged in manic headbanging

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A little band of fans who take part in frantic heavy-metal head-shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a specialised segment of a market or interest, a small distinct group.

clue.text: Singer given a flag endlessly backed by old artist

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its last letter
backed means sent backwards, so this pair is read in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written
to flag is to tire
O is the abbreviation for old
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock artist

explanation.surface: A vocalist presented with a banner supported by a veteran painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning tire. Rita Ora is a British pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rita Ora is a British pop singer known for chart hits in the 2010s, so she is a singer.

clue.text: Information about lake gained by runner once in Scottish village

indicators.note: about means around, so the information wraps round the lake

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
L is the map abbreviation for lake
Sebastian Coe was an Olympic middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: News about a loch reaching a former athlete in a Highland hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe is a British Olympic champion runner of the 1980s, later Lord Coe.
explanation.definitionFit: Glencoe is a village in the Scottish Highlands, site of the 1692 massacre.

clue.text: Restraint characteristic in second part of a book?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a trait is a characteristic
a dust jacket is the paper cover of a book

explanation.surface: Holding back as a typical feature of the middle section of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second part of a book' reads like a volume's middle section; the parts are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A straitjacket is a garment that restrains the arms, and figuratively anything that severely restricts.

clue.text: Obstreperous uncle moved to stand for society in credit

indicators.note: moved means shifted around, so these letters are rearranged
standing for something means replacing it, taking its place in the word

blocks.note: goods on trust are on credit
S is the abbreviation for society
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unruly uncle who has shifted to standing for a club while in the black.
explanation.walkthrough: In TRUST, the S is swapped for rearranged UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent means aggressively defiant, eager to fight or argue, much as obstreperous means noisily unruly.

clue.text: Prevalent notion in short by male in large-scale work

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its final letter
by means beside, so the male sits next to the notion
in places the pair inside the large-scale work

blocks.note: an epic is a long, grand work
a notion is an idea
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A widespread brief idea from a man inside a grand saga.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators share the word 'in': 'in short' trims, and the second 'in' places the pair inside the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidemic as an adjective means widespread, affecting many at once, which is what prevalent means.

clue.text: Writing, say, in country by journalist regarding a damaged joint?

indicators.note: in places the writing letter inside the country
by means next to, so the journalist follows

blocks.note: writing is one of the three Rs, each symbolised by R
Spain is a country
ED, editor, is the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter abroad writing about an injured knee or ankle.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; 'say' marks writing as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprained describes a joint injured by wrenching the ligaments, so it describes an injured joint.

clue.text: Source of inspiration in work of popular aged coach

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so take its opening letter
a work of the letters is something made out of them, rearranged

blocks.note: opening letter of inspiration
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly trainer whose popularity inspires others.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter sits in the jumble with the two words. Pep Guardiola is the Spanish football manager of Barcelona, Bayern and Manchester City.
explanation.definitionFit: Pep Guardiola is a celebrated football manager, and a manager in football is often called the coach.

clue.text: A bulge at sea revealing marine creature

indicators.note: at sea means all over the place, confused, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A swelling on the waves turns out to be a sea animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the marine picture but is the jumble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga is a white Arctic whale, and also a sturgeon, both creatures of the sea.

clue.text: Fellow on film interrupting, for example, snooker shot

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: say means for example
F is the abbreviation for fellow
ET is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A man in a movie breaking off mid-frame to play a cautious shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the fellow to the film so the two go in together as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a safety is a defensive shot that leaves the opponent no easy pot.

clue.text: A liberal, upper-class character recalled in horror novel

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
U means upper-class in British usage
a card is an eccentric person, a character

explanation.surface: A posh progressive figure remembered in a scary book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a figure in a novel, but it is CARD, an oddball. U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is Bram Stoker's 1897 Gothic horror novel about the vampire count.

clue.text: US actor facing right area to take in British plant

indicators.note: facing means in front of, so the actor comes first
the string absorbs the British letter, taking it inside

blocks.note: Richard Gere is an American actor
R is the abbreviation for right
A is the abbreviation for area
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star standing at the correct spot to admire a British flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The British letter goes inside the actor's name itself, after its third letter, not between the joined pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The gerbera is a daisy-like flowering plant, popular as a cut flower.

clue.text: Copy more profitable sandwiches

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer between its outer letters like a filling

blocks.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Imitation sandwiches turn a bigger profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like a noun for snacks, but it is a verb holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy of an original such as furniture or a print.

clue.text: Profitable source that includes cold type of meat

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside, so the cold letter goes within

blocks.note: a mine, as in gold mine, is a rich source
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A lucrative business selling chilled cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince is meat ground into small pieces, a form in which beef is commonly sold.

clue.text: Charge defended by English conservationists on river transport

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so the charge sits inside
on means next to, with the river joined at the end

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the National Trust is a British conservation charity
a rap is a criminal charge
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A fee charged by heritage bodies for ferrying people up the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' looks like boats; here it is a verb meaning to delight. The National Trust looks after historic sites in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with strong emotion, the same as to enrapture or delight.

clue.text: Trainees given poor grades in musical

indicators.note: in places the grades inside the musical's title

blocks.note: Cats is Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical
D and E are low exam grades

explanation.surface: Apprentices getting bad marks while appearing in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets are young people training for the armed forces or police, so they are trainees.

clue.text: Support a medic keeping very active by country's borders

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the doctor holds the letter inside
the borders of a word are its edges, so only its outer letters count

blocks.note: taken as written
a doc is a doctor
V is the abbreviation for very
A is the abbreviation for active
the outside letters of country

explanation.surface: Help from a doctor who keeps patients very active near the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocacy is public backing for a cause or person, so it is a form of support.
